whatItIs.text: Swimming crustaceans with muscular tails — the part we eat. 'Shrimp' and 'prawn' are kitchen words, not biology: taxonomists note the terms carry no fixed species meaning.

historyNote.text: Shrimp paddle forward on their swimmerets and escape backwards in tail flicks; they are among the most popular shellfish on earth, caught wild and farmed in staggering numbers — which is why bycatch and overfishing make the wild fisheries a real sustainability concern.

howToChoose.text: Buy frozen-at-sea when possible and thaw at home; shells should look clean and translucent with no ammonia smell. Size labels (16/20, 41/50) count shrimp per pound.

storage.text: Shellfish has the shortest fridge clock of all — keep it cold and cook within the rulebook's window, or freeze.
storage.note: raw-shellfish storage windows live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Shrimp overcook in a minute, so rescue them in hot pan at the last moment; cooked stragglers become fried rice, tacos, or a chilli-garlic pasta.

substitutions.note: same thing by most definitions; size matters more than name
